summary.text: 听 is the standardized simplified form of 聽, meaning “hear” or “listen.” Its current left–right structure is 口 and 斤. The same split appears in the received analysis of an older use meaning “smiling appearance,” but does not establish how 听 came to represent 聽.

formation.text: For the older word meaning “smiling appearance,” the received analysis treats 听 as phonosemantic: 口 depicts a mouth and contributes to the smiling sense, while 斤 is assigned a sound role. This analysis describes the older use, not how 听 came to represent 聽.

components.text: 口 is the left-hand component in the current form. In the received analysis of the older smiling-word use, it depicts a mouth contributing to the expression.
斤 is the right-hand component in the current form. The received analysis assigns it a sound role for the older smiling-word use; this does not establish why 听 came to represent 聽.

sound_limitation.text: The received Shuowen analysis assigns 斤 a phonetic role in the older smiling-word use. The reported Zhengzhang readings are compatible with that assignment, but do not independently establish that it reflects the graph’s original formation. The supplied Baxter–Sagart readings cover 聽, not the older 听 word; current Mandarin readings likewise do not establish the ancient relation.

sound.text: A Zhengzhang transcription gives readings for 斤 and 听, but the evidence does not match either 斤 reading to a specific reading of the older smiling-word 听.
A Zhengzhang transcription also gives an alternate reading for each graph; the evidence does not establish their correspondence.
In modern Mandarin, 斤 is jīn and 听 is tīng. This current reading pair does not establish an ancient sound relationship for the older smiling-word use.

history.text: The received Shuowen entry analyzes 听 in its older “smiling appearance” use as 口 with 斤 as phonetic. The curated image is identified as a modern redraw of 听 in Shuowen small-seal style; it does not establish a sequence of graphic changes.

A secondary proposal traces a vernacular form 𠯸, with 厅 as its sound element, to 听 through copying that assimilated 厅 to 斤. The intermediate form and this proposed graphic path have not been verified from primary manuscript evidence.

听 is the standardized simplified counterpart of 聽 and is attested for 聽 in Song–Yuan vernacular writing. The separate older smiling-word use does not show that its meaning developed into “hear” or “listen.”

uncertainties.text: The Han- and Tang-period literary examples attest the smiling sense but do not establish its first occurrence. The date and textual path by which 听 began representing 聽 are unresolved.

The proposed 𠯸-to-听 pathway and its 厅 sound element lack independent confirmation from primary manuscript evidence. The reported historical readings do not establish a matched comparison between 斤 and the older smiling-word 听.

senses.text: A cited Han-period literary example uses 听 for a smiling appearance. This attests the use by that period, but does not establish its first occurrence or original meaning.

senses.period: Song–Yuan vernacular use attested; beginning date unresolved
senses.text: 听 is used for “hear” and “listen” in present-day Chinese. Its use for the separate word 聽 is attested in Song–Yuan vernacular writing; the reason for this reuse is unresolved, and the proposed 𠯸/厅 account is not verified from primary manuscript evidence.

limitations.text: The smiling and hearing/listening uses are separately documented. No semantic development from “smiling appearance” to “hear” or “listen” is supported.

items.period: Shuowen small-seal-script tradition; modern digital redraw
items.tradition: Small seal script, labeled 小篆 / 說文‧口部 by the character-specific Xiaoxuetang record
items.caption: A Shuowen small-seal form associated with the older 听 word meaning “smiling appearance.”
items.alt: Black glyph on white. On the left, two upright strokes join a curved base to form an open-topped, U-shaped outline, crossed near the top by a horizontal line. A separate curved stroke on the right bends inward near its upper end.
items.selection_reason: The identified redraw shows a form associated with the old smiling-word entry; it is not the later use of 听 for 聽 and does not establish how that use arose.

limitations.text: This redraw is associated with the Shuowen small-seal tradition, not a dated archaeological specimen. It cannot establish the form’s artifact date or the graphic path by which 听 came to represent 聽; that use is attested in Song–Yuan vernacular sources, but its beginning and origin remain uncertain.
